questions.q: How is the free version of Microsoft Purview data governance different from a typical SaaS "free trial"?
options: It requires a credit card and expires after 30 days
It is a real, ongoing, automatically-available instance with no setup and no trial countdown
It only works for one hour per day
It is identical to the enterprise version in every way
questions.explain: Unlike a typical free trial, Purview's free version is a real, automatically-available instance an organization can keep using indefinitely to explore core data governance capabilities, not a time-limited trial.

questions.q: Which capability is enterprise-only, per this lesson's comparison table?
options: Browsing and searching data assets
Manually adding a description to an asset
Automated scanning for the hybrid data estate
Viewing the Catalog
questions.explain: Automated scans for the hybrid data estate, along with collections, automated classification, workflows, and support access, are all enterprise-only. The free version supports manual browsing and tagging only, via live view of a limited set of Azure sources.

questions.q: What does "upgrading" a Purview account from free to enterprise actually do?
options: It deletes all existing data and starts a brand-new account
It converts the existing free-tier instance into an enterprise one in place, with data preserved
It requires contacting Microsoft sales and signing a new contract before anything happens
It only changes the account's display name
questions.explain: Upgrading converts your existing instance in place — the data in the free version becomes available in the enterprise version automatically, and your portal experience stays the same.

questions.q: What is the practical difference between a Purview environment tag (like Production or Dev) and a Purview account's region?
options: There is no difference — they are the same setting

An environment tag is an optional label for your own organization that Purview doesn't enforce; a region is where metadata is physically stored, tied to your Entra tenant, and cannot be changed after account creation
A region is just a label; the environment tag controls where data is physically stored
Both can be freely changed at any time after the account exists
questions.explain: The environment tag is purely organizational, for your own clarity and billing — Purview doesn't enforce anything based on it. The region is where your account's metadata actually lives, and per this lesson, you cannot move a Purview account to a different region after creation.

questions.q: What capacity does a newly upgraded enterprise Purview account provision by default?
options: Unlimited capacity with no billing
1 capacity unit: 25 operations/second and 10 GB of metadata storage, with auto-scale available
100 capacity units pre-allocated
Capacity must be purchased separately before the upgrade can complete
questions.explain: The upgrade dialog shows that the enterprise tier provisions with 1 capacity unit (CU) by default — 25 operations per second and 10 GB of metadata storage — with auto-scale capabilities available afterward.
